release_oracle.method: driver.cpp runs 60 calls on ProgressLogger objects sharing the static depth: setLogType(CMD) and startProgress(5, 0) with setProgress below, on, between and above both ends (INT64_MIN, -1, 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, INT64_MAX) and two nextProgress; startProgress(2, 1) with setProgress 0-3; startProgress(0, 0) with setProgress 0 and 1 and nextProgress; nested ranges on two loggers (0..10 outside, 10..2 and 0..4 inside); a second start (5, 1) on an active CMD logger; endProgress without start; NONE and the default GUI factory with startProgress(5, 0). Every call runs under try/catch; the op log records the outcome (with exception name, message, file:line and function), the static depth after the call and the stdout byte offsets before and after it (stdout is a regular file, flushed and lseek'd).
release_oracle.dispatch: setProgress/nextProgress return early while last_invoke_ == time(nullptr) (ProgressLogger.cpp:244, :255). Before every set/next the driver polls time(nullptr) every 10 ms until it differs from that logger's last_invoke_ (read through a derived class), so each call lands in a new second; the op log's dispatch column records that last_invoke_ changed during the call ('forced' for all 31 set/next calls). The Rust replay advances its manual clock's wall_second at the same calls.
release_oracle.masking: Only the two timing texts of each '-- done [took X (CPU), Y (Wall)' line are replaced by <TIME>; every other byte, including carriage returns and indentation, is kept (extract.py).
release_oracle.repetition_result: all three runs exit 0 with empty stderr and byte-identical op logs; the masked per-call output is identical, and only the masked timing texts differ between runs
